Pendulum_lab is drifting or destabilizing: day 33 and day 40 excursions represent genuine instrumental deterioration or environmental coupling that is now recurring.

Data logging or timestamping error: pendulum_lab trial 233–238 (day 33) or their timestamps were recorded out of sequence or mislabeled, creating false scatter that will vanish upon inspection of raw logs

Coincidental numerical alignment in post-baseline period: random scatter in two independent instruments happened to align at a 3-day offset by chance, and the reported r = 0.966 reflects multiple-hypothesis testing without correction

Data logging or trial-sequencing error in pendulum_lab: trials 345–356 (or a subset thereof) were recorded out of temporal order or mislabeled with respect to day 40, creating false scatter that will disappear upon inspection of raw event logs and timestamps.

The r=0.966 pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs correlation at 3-day offset reflects data-logging corruption in one or both instruments, now suspected of having contaminated day 33 and day 40 readings as well.

Multiple-hypothesis testing bias: the r=0.966 correlation represents the maximum over many tested offset-pair combinations and should not be interpreted as a genuine signal without permutation testing explicitly corrected for the number of tests performed
